subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw add stable per-session attribution fields to official usage/status JSON now, and which surface owns them?
rationale: The code can derive some of the requested data, but field names, privacy policy for channel targets, and whether `status --usage --json` should become per-session are public API decisions rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Add safe attribution to sessions.usage
options.body: Extend `sessions.usage` with additive optional fields for session kind, cron job identity, channel label/kind, and runtime while keeping raw target ids redacted unless a separate opt-in is approved.

options.title: Keep status usage provider-only
options.body: Document `status --usage --json` as provider quota output and direct dashboards to `sessions.usage` for per-session attribution.

options.title: Defer broader JSON attribution
options.body: Handle the narrower CLI/TUI label issue first and leave dashboard-grade attribution for a later observability design pass.

recommendation.title: Add safe attribution to sessions.usage
recommendation.body: Extend `sessions.usage` with additive optional fields for session kind, cron job identity, channel label/kind, and runtime while keeping raw target ids redacted unless a separate opt-in is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest cross-surface history across status JSON, usage docs, and session/usage helpers, and the decision spans those public contracts.
